# Markdown Style Guide

## Authority

[STYLE-GUIDE.md](../../STYLE-GUIDE.md) is the source of truth for all content writing rules. This document covers structural and formatting conventions for Markdown files in this project.

## File Structure

Every article follows this template:

```markdown
---
title: "Article Title"
weight: N
---

# Article Title

| Key Fact | Value |
| -------- | ----- |
| ...      | ...   |

## Table of Contents (auto-generated by Hugo)

## Section 1

Content...

## Section 2

Content...

## Best Practices

- ...

## References

- [Official Doc Title](url)
```

## Formatting Conventions

- Use `--` for dashes, never em dash characters
- Use fenced code blocks with language identifiers (`bash, `toml, etc.)
- Use ATX-style headings (`##`) not setext-style (underlines)
- One blank line before and after headings, code blocks, and tables
- No trailing whitespace
- Files end with a single newline

## Tables

- Use tables for structured data: key facts, comparison matrices, decision guides
- Align table columns with spaces for readability in source
- Header row required

## Code Blocks

- Always specify the language: `bash, `toml, `yaml, `json, ```markdown
- Use inline code for file paths, command names, config keys, and short values
- Use code blocks for multi-line examples, command sequences, and file contents

## Links

- Use reference-style links for repeated URLs
- Use relative paths for internal wiki links
- External links go in the References section at the bottom

## Images and Diagrams

- Prefer ASCII diagrams over image files for architecture concepts
- If images are necessary, place them in `static/` and reference with absolute paths
